newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain urges Peru not to use force in standoff.
newsitem.headline: Spain urges Peru not to use force in standoff.

text.p: Spain has urged Peru to avoid using military force to end a hostage standoff, fearing it could lead to a massacre, Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Wednesday.

Heavily armed guerrillas were holding at least 200 hostages, many of them high-ranking officials, at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima. They have threatened to kill all unless the Peruvian government frees imprisoned fellow rebels.
Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar contacted Peru's President Alberto Fujimori and asked him to use psychological tactics to persuade the hostage-takers to stand down, Matutes said in a radio interview.

"We have just been in contact with President Fujimori to recommend...he use, to the extent possible, tactics of psychological attrition precisely to prevent a massacre in the event that security forces should intervene."
"Naturally what we want is the conflict to be resolved peacefully."
A foreign ministry official told Reuters Aznar had asked Fujimori to avoid using military force.
The Spanish charge d'affaires in Lima, Estanislao de Grandes, is among the hostages, the Spanish foreign ministry said.

The hostages include high-ranking diplomats who had been at a reception to honour the Japanese emperor's birthday when guerrillas from the Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) attacked the ambassador's residence.
